topic.title: Resetting a Locked-Out Linux User Account from Single-User Mode
topic.shortdesc: Use single-user mode to regain access by resetting a local Linux user password and restoring normal boot settings.

body.p: Confirm you have console or out-of-band access (iLO/iDRAC/IPMI) and authorization to perform account recovery. Reboot the system and interrupt the boot loader (GRUB) to edit the default kernel entry. Append a single-user or emergency boot parameter (for example, boot into emergency.target) and ensure the root filesystem can be remounted read-write. Boot with the modified parameters and obtain a root shell. Remount the root filesystem read-write if needed, then reset the affected user password with the system password tool. If SELinux is enabled, trigger a relabel on next boot when required by your distribution after changing authentication files. Restore the original boot loader entry (remove emergency/single-user parameters) and reboot normally. Validate login for the recovered account and review authentication logs for lockout causes.
